subject: Medistar pilot — routing, TIA mapping, and evidence tranche
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Holloway <sarah.holloway@medistar.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-01T17:12:00+00:00
Subject: Medistar pilot — routing, TIA mapping, and evidence tranche

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our runbook for the EU pilot, I wanted to put the immediate routing & evidence asks in one place so your procurement and legal teams can triage. High level: we expect to serve the pilot from our Frankfurt region with a UK-IDTA fallback for UK-resident users. Two practical items we should align on this week: 

1) TIA/DTIA mapping: can you confirm whether Medistar will accept a TIA (technical implementation appendix) linking our existing SCCs (EU) + the UK IDTA addendum, or if you require a separate DTIA form? We can produce both but prefer a single TIA that maps to each transfer mechanism.

2) Subprocessor evidence tranche: attached is our current subprocessor matrix (CSV) — we can provide per-subprocessor SOC/attestations or an aggregated evidence packet. Please advise which format your privacy team prefers and whether a secure SFTP or Drive handoff is needed.

Attached: Redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v1.csv (lightweight matrix), plus I can follow up with a one-pager comparing SCCs vs UK-IDTA if helpful.

Proposed next steps:
- Your team: confirm TIA vs DTIA preference + key deadline for pilot signoff (procurement requested "by Feb 10")
- Our team: finalize evidence packet and draft a TIA that references the SCCs and UK addendum
- Schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough (Jonas from infra will join)

If you want this bundled into DocuSign we can also prepare a signing packet once legal confirms the mechanism.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v1.csv

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side before we ingest your matrix: 

- Preference on TIA vs DTIA: Legal would prefer a single TIA that maps to both the SCCs and the UK IDTA addendum — that aligns with our internal playbook, but we need to review the draft language for the UK-specific clauses (data subject rights routing + escalation points).
- Evidence format: Procurement is OK with an aggregated evidence packet, but for the UK addendum sign-off they need per-subprocessor attestations for any subprocessors that process UK personal data.
- Timeline: Procurement has asked for internal signoff by Feb 10 UTC to keep the pilot start on Feb 20. If you can't hit that, tell us the earliest date you can deliver the TIA draft + per-subprocessor attestations.

Also: please call out any realtime routing fallback (e.g., if a request originates from the UK but is routed to EU compute) and whether logs will include routing provenance (we will need the provenance for our audit).

Attached: Medistar_TIA_Template.docx (our preferred template)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Holloway <sarah.holloway@medistar.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-02T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Medistar pilot — routing, TIA mapping, and evidence tranche

Hi Sarah —

Quick technical note to address the routing provenance and per-subprocessor question: 

- Routing provenance: our runtime tags requests at ingress with a routing_id and geography label (e.g., EU-FRA, UK-LON). These tags are persisted in request logs and can be returned in a sanitized audit bundle (timestamp + routing_id + model variant). We do not surface raw customer payloads in the provenance export — only metadata needed for audit.

- Fallback behavior: primary compute will be FR. For UK users we will attempt UK-local compute if capacity and compliance gating (customer tenancy config + UK addendum acceptance) are present; otherwise fallback to FR. We can include an optional policy to always route UK-origin to UK compute when requested.

- Subprocessors: attached is the matrix Kim sent; for the pilot the list of subprocessors that may process UK PD is: CloudCache Ltd. (edge CDN, UK POP), DataTransit Inc. (transit logging), and VectorOps Ltd. (model optimization). For each of these we can provide the following artifacts on request: SOC2 Type II summary, subprocessed-scoped dataflow map, and encryption-in-transit attestations. Expect the per-subprocessor artifacts in a single password-protected ZIP if that suits procurement.

Actionable: I can assemble the artifacts by EOD Feb 6 (PST) if Medistar confirms the evidence handoff method (SFTP vs Drive) and whether you need DocuSign-ready TIA language inserted.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v1.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Sarah / Mike / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the template, Sarah. Summary and agreed next steps below so we have a single reference: 

Summary of agreements so far:
- Medistar prefers a single TIA that maps our SCCs + the UK IDTA addendum; your legal will review draft UK-specific clauses.
- Procurement needs per-subprocessor attestations for any subprocessors processing UK personal data; Redwood will provide these as a password-protected ZIP.
- Audit/logging: Redwood will include routing provenance metadata in the audit bundle (no raw payloads).

Next steps / owners: 
- Redwood (Jonas): assemble per-subprocessor artifacts and post to the agreed handoff (SFTP or Drive) by EOD 2028-02-06. Attachment: Redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v1.csv (already shared).
- Redwood (Kim): draft the TIA that explicitly references: SCCs (EU), UK IDTA addendum, routing provenance logging, and fallback routing policy. I will circulate for legal comments by 2028-02-04.
- Medistar (Sarah / Mike / procurement): confirm preferred handoff ("drive" or "sftp") and confirm Feb 10 signoff target or provide alternative cutoff.
- Optional: schedule 30-min walkthrough the week of Feb 6 — propose Feb 7 11:00 GMT. Please confirm availability.

Attached for convenience: SCCs_vs_UK-IDTA-onepager.pdf (high-level comparison) — this is an internal one-pager that should make the legal review faster.

If OK I will: prepare the TIA draft and a DocuSign packet once you confirm handoff method and signoff date. Thanks everyone — looping Laura for any procurement escalations on our side.

Best regards,

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SCCs_vs_UK-IDTA-onepager.pdf
